text_source: As the Yamatans set foot on Tuskur soil, they\n
occupy the coast and set up a port as a\n
military foothold.
A great road leads inland from the shoreline--\n
an essential tool for transporting goods.
The road leads directly to the very heart of\n
Tuskur.
And so Yamato's invasion of the land of Tuskur\n
begins.
Tuskur, caught completely unawares, is forced\n
to take quick defensive action.
Soldiers are stationed at points throughout the\n
road, but they are unable to halt Yamato's\n
advance inland.
Soon, the Yamatan army succeeds in establishing\n
a fort along the road; a headquarters for\n
invasion forces.
That night, the three commanders--Dekopompo,\n
Munechika, and Raiko--hold a meeting within\n
the fortress.
The only other members present are their\n
retainers, who stand in the back.
All the other soldiers rejoice in their victory\n
by the large central bonfire with food, drink,\n
and song.
From time to time, the generals can hear the\n
soldiers' raucous laughter on the wind.
Their easy victories so far have buoyed their\n
spirits.
We are advancing swiftly, without question!\n
I would expect no less from the Pillar\n
Generals.
It seems we have little to fear from Tuskur.
Nyuh huh huh huh. So much for this "land where\n
god sleeps"... They're just a backwater little\n
island!
They pose no more of a threat than those\n
Uzurushan barbarians.
Well... P-Perhaps so...
We shall continue to ride this wave of triumph\n
all the way to the very heart of Tuskur!
Ah! Outstanding, Lord Dekopompo!\n
What great insight you have!
Of course I do. Here, you drink up too!
Ah, thank you so much, sir!
You treat this with far too much carelessness.
We still know very little about this land.\n
What is more, they still have the terrain\n
advantage.
If we rush heedlessly in, we may find the enemy\n
eager to welcome us with heavy casualties.
It is my opinion that we should proceed with\n
caution.
Well, well, well. Sounds to me like the strategy\n
of a coward.
I hardly believe such words come from one of the\n
proud Eight Pillar Generals of Yamato,\n
Munechika.
Being wary is all fine and good, but we shall\n
never seize victory if we withdraw into our\n
shells!
Anyhow, why don't we ask the opinion of our\n
marshal, Lord Raiko?
Munechika presents a valid point.
A general must never underestimate their enemy,\n
regardless of the circumstances.
Nyegh...?
Yet allowing caution in excess to slow down\n
our forces would also be a foolish mistake.
Whether it is a trap or not, I am sure that with\n
Dekopompo's valor, we may triumph over such\n
obstacles.
Yes! Yes, exactly!
Just as I expected, Raiko, it seems you have a\n
solid grasp of the greater picture!
Even so--
Munechika, I am the one appointed marshal for\n
this expedition. I am fully aware of my\n
responsibilities.
No doubt you have your own opinion on this, but\n
I will have you obey my decisions here.
Understood.
Nyoo hoo hoo! Then if you will excuse me, I have\n
much to prepare for. Bokoinante, Maroro, we go!
A-Aye, master.
I will excuse myself as well, then.
...Are you certain about this?
I believe Lady Munechika may be correct in\n
thinking that the enemy is preparing a trap...
It hardly matters.
I am getting rather sick and tired of having to\n
see that swine's bloated face.
If he aims to jump into the flames himself,\n
all the more convenient for me. He is more\n
than welcome to.
Of course, regardless of how well the swine is\n
roasted, I doubt anyone would find him\n
appetizing.
Haha... A cold assessment, milord...
Also...
Also?
If I play my hand correctly, I may even be able\n
to rid myself of that bothersome guardian.
...I see.
In truth, Munechika's fears are well-founded.
The Yamatan fortress had been set up precisely\n
where the Tuskur army had cleverly guided them\n
to.
Messenger
Reporting!
We have lost contact with units one, three, and\n
four!
Nyargh!?
We've also received reports that unit two has\n
been ambushed from the rear. Major casualties\n
sustained!
From the rear!? Wh-What is going on!?\n
Bokoinante! Where is the enemy coming from!?
I-I am not sure what is going on either...
Throughout the mountains is a network of hidden\n
pathways, utterly unknown to the Yamatans.
The Tuskur soldiers use these paths to go around\n
the Yamatan army, making their fortress useless.
And, on top of that...
O unhappy fortune!
The supply units bound from our landing point\n
have been set upon by enemy forces...
WHAT!?
There is only one traversable road from the\n
shore to the fortress.
Every Yamatan supply unit heading by road to the\n
fortress is soon attacked, and their supplies\n
taken.
So it has come to this... just as I had\n
expected.
We can neither take the offensive, nor retreat.\n
We are completely isolated from the rest of the\n
army.
We have yet to clash head-on, but if these\n
skirmishes continue, our forces will be whittled\n
down...
But who could have foreseen such difficulty...?\n
No... perhaps this is what she meant.
Miss Munechika...
Is there no way that the invasion of Tuskur\n
can be stopped?
I am afraid it is impossible. If our liege\n
commands it, we are duty-bound to carry out\n
his will.
But many people will die if this war begins.
Ah, yes... You have relations in Tuskur, if I\n
recall. I am sorry, but I have no power to\n
change this.
I see... I suppose there's not much left to say,\n
then.
Please be careful.\n
Come home safe...
Perhaps... this entire invasion was a mistake...
No... I cannot afford to let my resolve waver\n
now. I must find a way out of this dire\n
situation...
